title: Triangle-patch support in QuadLayout (3-valent singularity wedges)
description: Audit of TPatchEnumerator's PATCH-70 dump on Hand-30k shows the side-count histogram is [0,0,4,18,39,3,4,1,0,1,3,1,1,0,1,0]. We emit 39 quad patches (4 corners). The 18 triangle (3-corner) faces are 3-valent singularity wedges — Lyon paper Figure 5/6 shows these as legitimate small patches in the final layout. Currently we drop them. Implementation: (a) add Variant.TRIANGLE to QuadLayoutPatch (or a separate TrianglePatch record), (b) update QuadLayoutExtractor to emit 3-corner faces as triangle patches, (c) audit downstream consumers (LyonMetrics, Coons evaluator, DSL emitter PATCH-57) to handle them. Adding 18 triangles to Hand-30k jumps #P from 39 to 57 (still vs metriko's 96 — the remaining 39 are big multi-corner faces that may be DCEL boundary-walk artifacts, separate diagnostic ticket).
definition-of-done: QuadLayout exposes triangle patches; LyonMetrics counts them in #P; Hand-30k #P jumps from 39 to ~57 in the benchmark output.
testing-plan: Toy: synthetic 3-valent singularity fixture with 3 wedges → #P = 3 triangles. Hand-30k regression: #P >= 50.
